ledger.x: 1920, 26 August: the Kirghiz ASSR is established as "an autonomous republic within the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic", on the steppe north of the Turkestan ASSR.
1920, 26 August: the Kirghiz ASSR is established as "an autonomous republic within the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic".
1924, October: the Syr Darya and Semirechye lands of the Turkestan ASSR (dissolved 27 October 1924) pass to the Kirghiz ASSR.
1925, 15-19 April: the Kirghiz ASSR is renamed the Kazak ASSR.
1929: Alma-Ata is designated the new capital in place of Kzyl-Orda (the page: "in 1927 or 1929.
1936, 5 December: the Kazak ASSR is detached from the RSFSR and becomes the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic, a union republic of the USSR.
1936, 5 December: "on 5 December 1936 it was elevated to the status of a Union-level republic".
1991, 10 December: the Kazakh SSR is renamed the Republic of Kazakhstan; it had declared sovereignty on 25 October 1990.
1991, 16 December: Kazakhstan declares independence, "the last republic to secede from the USSR"; the Soviet Union ends 26 December.
